ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening of all UBOs, directors, and signatories against the Korean Financial Intelligence Unit (FIU) PEP list, the United Nations Security Council Consolidated List, OFAC SDN List, EU Consolidated Financial Sanctions List, and the Korean government's own sanctions list (e.g., Ministry of Foreign Affairs). Enhanced due diligence (EDD) is required for any PEP, including foreign PEPs, family members, and close associates. Continuous monitoring via automated screening tools and manual review is mandated. Any positive hit triggers immediate reporting to the FIU and suspension of the incorporation process until clearance. The screening must be documented and retained for at least five years post-incorporation.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Supreme Court Registry Office (대법원 등기국) – i-REG Online Portal (인터넷등기소)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Company names must be in Korean (Hangul) script. English names are permitted as secondary names but must be transliterated phonetically into Hangul for registration. The name must consist of a distinctive element, a business purpose descriptor, and a legal form suffix (e.g., '유한회사' for LLC). The name must not be identical or confusingly similar to any existing registered entity. Four-tier naming conventions: (1) distinctive word, (2) business type, (3) legal form, (4) optional English transliteration.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: If a name is rejected, the applicant may file a written appeal with the Supreme Court Registry Office within 14 days of rejection. The appeal must include the proposed name, the reason for rejection, and a legal argument demonstrating compliance with the Commercial Act and the Name Clearance Guidelines. The Registry must respond within 30 days. If the appeal is denied, the applicant may seek judicial review in the Administrative Court. Alternatively, the applicant may submit a revised name with a new reservation request. The appeal process is governed by the Commercial Registration Act and the Administrative Litigation Act.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Virtual offices and commercial mailboxes are generally permissible for registration purposes, but they are subject to strict scrutiny by the National Tax Service (NTS) and financial institutions. For a gaming company with global operations, a virtual office may be accepted if it provides a physical address, mail handling, and a registered agent. However, banks and payment processors (e.g., Apple, Google) may require a physical presence for KYC and AML compliance. The NTS may reject a virtual office if it is deemed to lack commercial substance, especially for VAT and corporate tax purposes. It is recommended to lease a serviced office or co-working space with a dedicated meeting room to demonstrate substance.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: The NTS and the Supreme Court Registry may conduct unannounced physical inspections to verify the existence of the registered office. The likelihood is moderate (30-40%) for newly formed entities, especially if the business is high-revenue or cross-border. Checklist: (1) Physical signage with company name, (2) Access to office during business hours, (3) Presence of employees or a registered agent, (4) Availability of corporate records and books, (5) Compliance with fire and safety regulations. Failure to pass an inspection can result in fines, revocation of registration, and adverse tax consequences.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Commercial Act of the Republic of Korea (상법), Articles 51-2 through 51-74 (Limited Liability Company), and Article 287-2 (Application of provisions to LLCs); Framework Act on the Registration of Real Estate and Corporations, Article 3 (Commercial Registration)
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Commercial Registration Division, District Court (법인등기과, 지방법원) having jurisdiction over the registered office address; for online filing, the Supreme Court's Commercial Registration Information System (인터넷등기소)
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Articles of Incorporation (정관) and Application for Corporation Registration (법인등기신청서) submitted to the court registry
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: None. The Commercial Act does not impose a minimum paid-up capital for a Yuhan Hoesa (LLC). However, the total capital must be stated in the Articles of Incorporation and fully paid in at the time of incorporation. The capital must be deposited into a bank account in the name of the company or a designated escrow account, and a certificate of deposit must be submitted to the registry. No blocked escrow period applies after registration.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLUTION OF THE SOLE INCORPORATOR AND FIRST BOARD OF DIRECTORS OF [COMPANY NAME] (YUHAN HOESA) TAKEN IN WRITING ON [DATE] AT [TIME] AT [PLACE]. WHEREAS, the undersigned, being the sole incorporator and the initial director of [COMPANY NAME] (the 'Company'), a limited liability company (Yuhan Hoesa) to be incorporated under the Commercial Act of the Republic of Korea, desires to adopt the following resolutions to effectuate the incorporation and initial governance of the Company. NOW, THEREFORE, BE IT RESOLVED, that the Articles of Incorporation of the Company, as previously drafted and reviewed, are hereby approved and adopted in their entirety, and the incorporator is authorized to execute and file the same with the competent court registry. RESOLVED FURTHER, that the initial capital of the Company, as set forth in the Articles of Incorporation, shall be subscribed in full by the sole shareholder, and the payment of such capital shall be made by deposit into a bank account designated by the incorporator, with the certificate of deposit to be submitted to the registry as required by law. RESOLVED FURTHER, that the registered office of the Company shall be established at [Address], Republic of Korea, and the Company shall maintain its principal place of business at such address, with the authority to change the registered office upon resolution of the board and amendment of the Articles of Incorporation. RESOLVED FURTHER, that the following individuals are hereby appointed as the first statutory officers of the Company: [Name] as Representative Director (대표이사) and [Name] as Auditor (감사), each to serve until the first annual general meeting of shareholders or until their successors are duly elected and qualified. RESOLVED FURTHER, that the Representative Director is hereby authorized to open and maintain bank accounts in the name of the Company, to execute all banking documents, and to designate authorized signatories for the purpose of receiving payments from Apple App Store and Google Play Store, and to manage all corporate funds in accordance with applicable law. RESOLVED FURTHER, that the Representative Director is hereby authorized to execute, deliver, and file all necessary documents, including but not limited to the registration application, tax registration, and any other filings required by the Korean tax authorities, the Financial Services Commission, or any other regulatory body, to commence the Company's business operations. RESOLVED FURTHER, that the Company shall adopt a corporate seal (법인인감) and shall register the same with the registry, and the Representative Director shall have custody of the seal and shall use it only in accordance with these resolutions and applicable law. RESOLVED FURTHER, that the Company shall indemnify and hold harmless each officer and director to the fullest extent permitted by law, and shall procure director and officer liability insurance as deemed appropriate. RESOLVED FURTHER, that the Representative Director is authorized to engage legal counsel, accountants, and other professional advisors as necessary to complete the incorporation process and to ensure ongoing compliance with Korean corporate and tax laws. RESOLVED FURTHER, that all actions taken by the incorporator and the director prior to the date of this resolution in connection with the formation of the Company are hereby ratified, approved, and confirmed in all respects. RESOLVED FURTHER, that this resolution may be executed in counterparts, each of which shall be deemed an original, and all of which together shall constitute one and the same instrument. RESOLVED, that the foregoing resolutions shall be effective immediately upon adoption. ADOPTED this [DATE] by the unanimous written consent of the sole shareholder and the first director, in accordance with the Commercial Act and the Articles of Incorporation. [SIGNATURE] [NAME] [TITLE]

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Draft and Notarize Articles of Incorporation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Notary Public (공증인) and the Commercial Registration Information System (인터넷등기소) for subsequent filing
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: The incorporator must draft the Articles of Incorporation (정관) in Korean, specifying the company name, purpose (including MMORPG publishing and global digital content distribution), registered office address, total capital, number of shares or units, and the names of the initial director and auditor. The Articles must be notarized by a Korean notary public to verify the identity and legal capacity of the incorporator. The notarized Articles must then be submitted to the court registry via the online system or in person. Ensure that the company name is approved by the registry to avoid duplication. The notarization fee is approximately KRW 50,000, and the registry filing fee is KRW 120,000. The Articles must be signed by the incorporator and the notary's seal affixed.
required_dossiers: Identification documents of the incorporator (passport or Korean ID)
Power of attorney if filed by an agent
Certificate of name reservation (상호예약증명서) if obtained
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the registry issues a query or suspension, the incorporator must correct the Articles or provide additional documentation within 14 days. If the name is rejected, a new name must be reserved and the Articles amended. Legal counsel can assist in resolving any substantive objections.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Deposit Paid-in Capital and Obtain Certificate of Deposit
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Commercial Bank in the Republic of Korea (e.g., Kookmin, Shinhan, Woori) or a licensed escrow agent
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: The incorporator must open a temporary bank account in the name of the company (or a designated escrow account) and deposit the full amount of the stated capital. The bank will issue a certificate of deposit (납입증명서) confirming the deposit. This certificate is a mandatory attachment to the registration application. The deposit must be made before the registration application is submitted. The bank account will be converted to a corporate account after registration. The capital can be in Korean Won or foreign currency, but the certificate must state the amount in KRW. No minimum capital is required, but the amount must be reasonable and sufficient for the company's initial operations.
required_dossiers: Certificate of deposit (납입증명서) issued by the bank
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank refuses to open the account or issue the certificate, the incorporator must provide additional due diligence documents, such as a business plan or source of funds declaration. If the deposit is returned or the account is closed, the process must be restarted with a new deposit.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: File Application for Corporation Registration with the Court
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Supreme Court Commercial Registration Information System (인터넷등기소) or the District Court Registry (법원등기과) in the jurisdiction of the registered office
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: The incorporator or a licensed legal representative must submit the application for registration (법인등기신청서) to the court registry, either online or in person. The application must include the notarized Articles, the certificate of deposit, the power of attorney (if applicable), and the identification of the director and auditor. The registry will review the application for compliance with the Commercial Act. Upon approval, the court will issue a certificate of registration (법인등기사항증명서) and assign a corporate registration number. The registration must be completed within 14 days of the notarization of the Articles. The court will also register the corporate seal (법인인장) if submitted.
required_dossiers: Identification of the director and auditor
Power of attorney (if filed by an agent)
Corporate seal registration form (인영신고서) and seal impression
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the registry issues a correction order (보정명령), the applicant must cure the deficiencies within 14 days. If the application is rejected, the applicant may appeal to the court or file a new application. Common issues include incomplete documents, mismatched information, or failure to pay fees. Legal counsel can expedite the cure.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Obtain Business Registration Certificate from the National Tax Service
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Local District Tax Office (세무서) under the National Tax Service (국세청)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: After the court registration, the company must apply for a business registration certificate (사업자등록증) from the local tax office within 20 days of the registration date. The application must be submitted online via the HomeTax system (홈택스) or in person. The company must provide the corporate registration certificate, the Articles of Incorporation, and the identification of the representative director. The tax office will issue a business registration number (사업자등록번호) and a certificate. This number is required for all tax filings, VAT, and corporate income tax. The company must also register for VAT if its annual revenue exceeds KRW 80 million, but for a newly formed company, it can register voluntarily.
required_dossiers: Lease agreement for the registered office (if applicable)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the tax office requests additional information, the company must provide it within 10 days. If the application is delayed, the company may be subject to penalties for late registration. The company can file an appeal with the National Tax Service if the registration is wrongfully denied.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Open Corporate Bank Account and Register for Electronic Tax Invoices
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Commercial Bank and the National Tax Service (HomeTax system)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: The company must open a corporate bank account in the name of the company, using the business registration certificate and the corporate seal. The bank will verify the company's existence and the representative director's identity. The account is necessary for receiving payments from Apple App Store and Google Play Store. Additionally, the company must register for electronic tax invoice (전자세금계산서) issuance through the HomeTax system, which is mandatory for all VAT-registered businesses. The company must also obtain a corporate seal certificate (인감증명서) from the registry for banking and contractual purposes.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank refuses to open the account due to AML concerns, the company must provide additional documentation, such as a business plan, source of funds, or a reference from a Korean law firm. If the HomeTax registration fails, the company must contact the tax office to resolve technical issues.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Not Applicable - The company is engaged in software publishing (ISIC 5820) and does not operate physical manufacturing, chemical, assembly, or warehousing facilities. No industrial licensing is required.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Not Applicable - No operating license is required for digital MMORPG publishing under Korean law, except for standard business registration and, if applicable, a game rating certificate from the Game Rating and Administration Committee (GRAC) for distribution in Korea, which is not a physical license.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Not Applicable - No physical operations, so the Ministry of Environment (환경부) and the Korea Environment Corporation (한국환경공단) have no jurisdiction.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt - The company's activities are purely digital and do not trigger any EIA requirements under the Environmental Impact Assessment Act (환경영향평가법).
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Not Applicable - No wastewater, VOC, or hazardous waste generation. The company must only comply with general waste disposal regulations for office waste, which are handled by municipal waste services.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Not Applicable - The company does not operate a physical facility requiring fire safety certification or structural load inspections. However, the company must comply with the Occupational Safety and Health Act (산업안전보건법) for its office premises, including basic fire safety measures such as fire extinguishers and evacuation plans, which are typically verified by the local fire department during routine inspections. The company must also register with the Ministry of Employment and Labor (고용노동부) for workplace safety insurance (산재보험) for its employees.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: National Tax Service (NTS) of the Republic of Korea through the Home Tax Service (HTS) online portal (hometax.go.kr); export declarations are filed at the Korea Customs Service through the UNI-PASS electronic customs system.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: A foreign non-resident entity wishing to operate a Korean Yuhan Hoesa must register the domestic entity with the competent district tax office within 20 days of business commencement. The process includes: (1) filing an Application for Business Registration with the district tax office via HTS or in person; (2) submitting the certificate of incorporation, articles of incorporation, certificate of foreign registration or evidence of foreign entity existence, foreign investment notification certificate (if applicable), domestic business place lease or ownership proof, identification of the representative director, and a power of attorney for the local tax agent if one is appointed; (3) receiving the 10-digit Business Registration Number (business entity registration number) that functions simultaneously as the corporate TIN and VAT identification number. A foreign non-resident corporation without a domestic place of business that is liable for Korean VAT on electronic services to Korean customers must instead complete the NTS simplified foreign business operator registration through a tax representative and receive a separate foreign business registration number for VAT filing.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: None. A Yuhan Hoesa is classified as a domestic corporation under the Korean Corporate Tax Act and is subject to entity-level taxation on worldwide income; Korean tax law does not provide a check-the-box election or an analogous entity classification election for a Yuhan Hoesa to be treated as a pass-through entity. No domestic hybrid-mismatch election exists, although cross-border structures remain subject to the tax treaty limitations and OECD BEPS anti-hybrid rules.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Value-Added Tax (VAT) under the Value-Added Tax Act
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: KRW: There is no general turnover registration threshold for a domestic Yuhan Hoesa; every business operator must register with the NTS before commencing business. A simplified taxpayer regime may apply only to certain small individual businesses with annual taxable supplies not exceeding KRW 80,000,000, but this is an administrative simplification and does not create an exemption from VAT registration. Non-resident electronic service suppliers without a fixed place of business may use the NTS simplified foreign business registration procedure.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Electronic tax invoicing is mandatory through the NTS Home Tax Service (HTS) e-tax invoice system. A VAT-registered supplier must issue an e-tax invoice for each taxable supply and transmit the e-tax invoice data to NTS electronically using HTS-approved API integration or the HTS portal by the statutory filing deadline; paper tax invoices are not generally permitted. Cash receipts for consumer sales are processed through the NTS cash-receipt system and transmitted to NTS at the point of sale. There is no separate physical anti-fraud fiscal stamp, but the NTS continuously reconciles e-tax invoices, cash receipts, credit card settlement data, and customs data to enforce VAT compliance. For MMORPG sales through Apple App Store and Google Play, the responsible VAT invoice issuer is determined by the contract structure: if the app store is the supplier/reseller, the platform handles Korean VAT; if the Yuhan Hoesa is the supplier and the store only processes payment, the Yuhan Hoesa must issue e-tax invoices and report the supplies through HTS.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Zero-rating under the Value-Added Tax Act applies to goods exported from Korea and to services supplied to a foreign recipient that are performed or used wholly outside Korea and paid for in foreign currency. For an MMORPG publisher, zero-rating is available for revenue derived from non-Korean users where the game is consumed outside Korea, the contract is with the foreign end user or foreign platform, the app-store territory reports and settlement statements identify foreign jurisdictions, and the foreign currency proceeds are remitted to Korea. Supplies to users in Korea (including digital goods sold through Korean app-store storefronts to local customers) are domestic supplies subject to 10% VAT and cannot be zero-rated. The zero-rating claim must be supported by export and foreign exchange evidence at the time of filing.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Korea Customs Service UNI-PASS electronic Export Declaration (full export clearance record)
Bill of Lading (sea) or Air Waybill (air) signed by the carrier
Foreign Exchange Bank settlement/receipt confirmation (bank-issued foreign exchange receipt confirmation, equivalent to an Inward Remittance Confirmation)
App store platform settlement statements and territory-specific sales reports (for digital game exports)
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: The NTS cross-matches the UNI-PASS export declaration data, VAT return zero-rated entries, and foreign exchange bank receipt records. If any statutory document is absent, inconsistent, or fabricated, the 0% rate is revoked and VAT is assessed at the standard 10% rate on the gross supply. Additional tax penalties are imposed under the Framework Act on National Taxes and the Value-Added Tax Act, generally 20% of the underpaid tax for negligent underreporting and up to 40% for intentional or fraudulent underreporting, plus daily interest for late payment. A false zero-rating claim can also trigger criminal liability under the Punishment of Tax Evaders Act, and any refund previously claimed is clawed back with interest from the original refund date.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Bank of Korea (The Central Bank of the Republic of Korea), acting as the foreign exchange information administrator under the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act delegated by the Ministry of Economy and Finance
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: South Korea operates a liberalized foreign exchange system under the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act and the Foreign Investment Promotion Act. Current account transactions, including software royalties, influencer payments, subscriber revenues, and international settlement of digital content, are generally freely convertible through designated foreign exchange banks with reporting obligations. Capital account transactions are subject to a higher level of administrative scrutiny; foreign direct investment in the Korean LLC must be declared to the Ministry of Trade, Industry and Energy or a delegated bank, and the subscribed capital must be deposited into a domestic temporary account to obtain a foreign-investment registration certificate. Dividend distributions and profit remittances to non-resident shareholders are permissible but require evidence of audited net profits, tax clearance on Korean corporate tax and dividend withholding tax, board payment resolution, and the absence of outstanding obligations. Foreign currency proceeds from digital MMORPG sales, including Apple App Store and Google Play payouts, are usually received in USD and can be retained in foreign currency bank accounts or sold on exchange. Surrender requirements are minimal; no blanket income conversion is mandatory. However, the Ministry of Economy and Finance can impose temporary conversion ceilings or use safety clauses under IMF-style early warning conditions. Special attention should be paid to split treatment between goods-related trade settlements and services payments in the automated reporting system to avoid enforcement penalties.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Under the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act, exporters of digital content and software must obtain settlement of export proceeds within 180 days from the date of export; the original due date is 90 days with a single 90-day extension upon application to the designated bank. Export receipts may be credited to a foreign currency account without any statutory conversion ratio for ordinary service and software exports; this means the mandatory surrender/convertibility ratio is 0% at standard operating conditions. In a financial imbalance emergency, the Ministry of Economy and Finance, via the Bank of Korea, may impose a temporary mandatory conversion requirement up to 30% of export receipts, with prior public notice. The exporter must file a monthly reporting of outstanding export claims and may be required to transfer all settlement foreign currency to an onshore foreign currency account maintained with a designated foreign exchange bank.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Foreign Investment Capital Escrow Account and Basic Operational Won Account

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Offshore digital EMI viability is Low for primary treasury operations. Under the Electronic Financial Transactions Act, a non-bank payment service provider must obtain a license from the Financial Services Commission to handle Korean won deposits or receive electronic payments in Korea. Offshore fintech EMIs such as Revolut, Wise, and Payoneer are not licensed deposit-taking institutions in Korea and cannot legally operate a Korean won business account for an onshore LLC. Their utility is limited to receiving inbound cross-border royalty or payout settlement from Apple, Google, or foreign publishers in USD or EUR, and even that channel must be routed through a domestic intermediary bank subject to foreign exchange reporting. We recommend using a domestic Tier-1 bank for all statutory capital, payroll, and corporate disbursement accounts; an offshore EMI may be used after approval as a supplementary collection pocket, but not for capital verification, tax filing, or FX hedging.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: South Korean banks and the Korea Financial Intelligence Unit require, under the Real Name Financial Transaction Act, face-to-face or equivalent electronic identity verification for all signatories when opening corporate bank accounts. Domestic statutory directors may visit the branch with original corporate documents, company seal certificates, and ID. Non-resident directors must provide a notarized and apostilled passport copy, corporate resolution, and power of attorney; remote opening can be processed through video identification only if the director possesses a Korean real-name mobile phone certificate or a bank-approved digital identity alternative. In practice, at least one authorised signatory must attend a physical branch interview in Seoul for first-time foreign Korean LLC accounts. A remote consular proxy opening is generally not permitted as a replacement for the branch interview; however, once the bank relationship is established, additional signatories can be added through notarised powers of attorney and video confirmation. We advise the foreign beneficial owner to travel to Seoul for one in-branch interview and to prepare apostilled founding documents before account application.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Undeclared foreign shareholders and opaque beneficial ownership in a foreign-owned Korean LLC
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: A current corporate registry extract from the Korean court registry office; certificate of incorporation; articles of association; a complete beneficial ownership chain back to natural persons; a notarised and apostilled declaration of ultimate beneficial owner executed by each foreign shareholder; director passport copies; and if the foreign shareholder is itself a legal entity, audited financial statements and a corporate register with shareholder listing.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Unclear source of funds for initial capital injection and for subsequent deposits sourced from App Store or Google Play earnings
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Foreign Investment Report certificate or a domestic bank registered foreign-investment record; remittance advice and exchange contract for each inbound wire; Bank of Korea settlement receipts; investor bank statements for the preceding 12 months; profit and loss statement for the Korean LLC; relevant tax returns; Apple App Store Connect and Google Play Console payment summaries; and contractual documentation showing the patent, trademark, and digital content rights ownership structure.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Gaming transaction red flags due to virtual item trading, user-to-user transfers, and possible third-party chargebacks
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Compliance policies for anti-fraud and anti-money laundering; know-your-customer data for high-value players; transaction monitoring and suspicious activity reporting logs; records of chargeback and refund requests with mitigations; in-game virtual item conversion logic; evidence of restriction policies for unverified prosumers; and user agreements explicitly prohibiting money laundering.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Sanctions exposure, high-risk jurisdiction reach, and export declaration mismatches due to a global MMORPG distribution network
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Sanctions screening lists (UN, OFAC, and EU) applied to institutional counterparties and payment processors; geolocation and IP verification demonstrating compliance with sanctions; digital distribution contracts excluding prohibited jurisdictions; compliance certification with Google Play and App Store payment rails; and Korea Customs Service or Ministry trade documentation showing service-related export declarations with the proper code classification for software royalties.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: For inbound capital contributions, the Korean LLC must open a temporary receipt account at a designated foreign exchange bank and file a foreign-investment report to the Ministry of Trade, Industry and Energy, or the bank, before remittance. The investor should send the wire via SWIFT MT103 using the foreign exchange purpose code for direct equity investment by a non-resident in a domestic company, with the foreign investment report number in the remittance information field and the Korean LLC as the beneficiary. After the capital arrives, the bank will issue a Foreign Investment Capital Verification Report and a Foreign-Invested Enterprise registration certificate; the temporary capital escrow account is then converted into the operating account. For software revenue settlement, Apple and Google payouts enter via SWIFT MT103 with the service-related foreign exchange code for software royalties, not as capital. All cross-border flows must be filed in the Bank of Korea automated reporting system within the prescribed deadline.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Outbound payments for MMORPG developers, contractors, license fees, and marketing vendors should be initiated onshore through SWIFT MT103 for services and royalties, using the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act service payment purpose code. For physical merchandise such as boxed game copies or peripherals, a commercial letter of credit is acceptable when the transaction is trade-backed; for digital content, an L/C is rarely used. Documentary collections (documents against payment and documents against acceptance) are possible but not recommended for recurring royalty payments because digital transactions lack a transport document trail; SWIFT MT103 with invoice and contract is the standard clearing rail. For payouts from Apple and Google, each daily settlement file should be matched to the player-facing tax records and to the revenue reports in App Store Connect and Play Console. All outbound won wires must clear through the Bank of Korea Won-based electronic settlement system, while USD and major currency wires clear through the onshore treasury foreign currency settlement network to correspondent banks.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Deliverable forward exchange contracts with an onshore Bank of Korea licensed foreign exchange bank, available only when the Korean LLC can evidence the underlying USD/KRW trade, royalty, or service exposure and the contract maturity is aligned with the corresponding transaction date.

Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) are permitted for hedging the same underlying exposure when the settlement must remain in Korean won or the onshore bank cannot deliver foreign currency; NDFs must be booked with an onshore entity and are limited to real-demand exposure documentation under the Financial Supervisory Service principle of legitimate hedging.

Cross-currency swaps are permissible for long-term foreign currency funding or long-dated license receivables where the notional is matched to the USD revenue stream from Apple App Store or Google Play, and anti-abuse rules prohibit swap-only speculation; the swap must be tied to a specific balance sheet asset or liability.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Corporate Income Tax Return and Corporate Tax Base Computation Statement
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: National Tax Service (NTS) - competent district tax office of the registered business place
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 3 months after fiscal year-end; for a calendar-year company, on or before 31 March of the following year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing/non-filing attracts additional corporate tax of 20% where unpaid tax does not exceed KRW 100 million, or 40% where it does; under-reporting attracts 10% to 40% of the under-reported tax; late payment accrues delinquent interest at approximately 0.025% per day (c. 9.125% per annum). Persistent non-settlement may trigger seizure of assets, commercial registration enforcement, forced closure, and, in extreme dormancy cases, administrative strike-off proceedings by the registry court or NTS.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Local Income Tax (Surtax) Return and Payment on Corporate Income Tax
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Local government (si/gun/gu or metropolitan/provincial authority) through the integrated local tax filing portal
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 1 month after the corporate income tax return due date; for a calendar-year company, on or before 30 April of the following year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Additional local tax of 20% to 40% for non-filing or under-reporting, plus daily late-payment interest of about 0.025%. Unpaid local surtax triggers enforcement against bank accounts and other property, and the absence of tax clearance certificates can block corporate transactions and public bidding; severe delinquency may lead to the suspension of the business master data and administrative collection measures.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Value-Added Tax Preliminary Return and Payment - First Quarter (January through March)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: National Tax Service (NTS) - via the Home Tax Service (HTS) electronic portal
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: On or before 25 April following the close of the first quarter
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to file/pay VAT exposes the company to additional VAT of 20% (or up to 40% for intentional omission), plus 0.025% per day late-payment interest. Continued non-filing may result in estimated assessment by the NTS, collection enforcement, and a negative compliance record affecting licensing and payment-channel agreements.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Value-Added Tax Final Return and Payment - First Half (January through June)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: National Tax Service (NTS) - via the Home Tax Service (HTS) electronic portal
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: On or before 25 July following the close of the first half
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing/non-payment attracts additional VAT of 20% to 40%, plus daily interest at 0.025%; under-reporting penalties of 10% to 40% apply; enforcement includes asset seizure and banking account freezes. Persistent non-performance can be treated as tax evasion and may lead to criminal complaints and administrative winding-up.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Value-Added Tax Preliminary Return and Payment - Third Quarter (July through September)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: National Tax Service (NTS) - via the Home Tax Service (HTS) electronic portal
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: On or before 25 October following the close of the third quarter
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to file or pay results in additional VAT of 20% (or 40% for deliberate non-reporting) plus daily delinquent interest of 0.025%; continued failure may trigger estimated assessment, forced collection, and the optional nullification of the business registration for tax purposes.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Value-Added Tax Final Return and Payment - Second Half (July through December)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: National Tax Service (NTS) - via the Home Tax Service (HTS) electronic portal
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: On or before 25 January following the close of the second half
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Non-filing or non-payment of the final VAT return exposes the company to additional VAT of 20%-40%, interest of about 0.025% per day, under-reporting penalties, and possible criminal enforcement. Persistent delinquency may lead to business closure enforced by the NTS and an administrative strike-off of the dormant company if other statutory filings are also ignored.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual General Meeting of Members and Adoption of Annual Financial Statements and Profit Appropriation
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Not a government filing; minutes and financial statements must be retained in the statutory corporate registers and made available to tax authorities and auditors
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 6 months after the fiscal year-end; for a calendar-year company, on or before 30 June of the following year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to convene the members' meeting within the statutory window constitutes a breach of the Korean Commercial Act. Responsible directors/managers are subject to civil liability, court-imposed administrative fines, and possible disqualification; a systematically dormant company may be judicially dissolved or struck off from the company registry by the competent district court.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Foreign-Invested Company Annual Business Status Report (if any non-resident shareholder holds a reportable foreign investment)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Ministry of Trade, Industry and Energy (MOTIE) through Korea Trade-Investment Promotion Agency (KOTRA)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 90 days after fiscal year-end, or as prescribed by the Foreign Investment Promotion Act and its Enforcement Decree
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to submit or filing false data may attract administrative fines under the Foreign Investment Promotion Act and can impair the treatment of the company as a foreign-invested enterprise; it does not trigger an automatic strike-off, but continued non-reporting may lead to administrative enforcement and cancellation of foreign-investment incentives.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Under the Korean Act on External Audit of Stock Companies, etc., a Yuhan Hoesa (limited liability company) is statutorily required to engage an independent certified CPA as external auditor when: (a) its total assets as of the immediately preceding fiscal year-end equal or exceed KRW 10 billion (approximately USD 7.5 million); (b) it is an issuer of listed securities or a public-interest corporation; (c) it is a financial institution, e-money issuer, payment company, or crypto-asset service provider, regardless of size; (d) it belongs to a large-scale business group subject to the Monopoly Regulation and Fair Trade Act; or (e) it is expressly designated as an audit-subject company under industry-specific legislation (including digital-content/payment-ecosystem licensing rules that require audited financial statements). The quantitative tests are computed on statutory financial statements prepared under the applicable accounting framework. Other balance-sheet, turnover, or headcount tests may be imposed by investors or payment rails (Apple App Store and Google Play) as a commercial prerequisite for operating agreements.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: For companies subject to mandatory external audit, Korea has fully adopted International Financial Reporting Standards (K-IFRS). Unlisted companies, including most Yuhan Hoesa entities, may use Korean Generally Accepted Accounting Principles (K-GAAP) or the Korean SMEs Accounting Standards (K-SMEs) when permitted; voluntarily, they may apply K-IFRS. The selected framework must be applied consistently, and any change must be disclosed and accounted for in accordance with the applicable standard.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: South Korea does not impose a standalone annual beneficial-owner confirmation return on a standard Yuhan Hoesa under ordinary corporate law. The company must, however: (1) maintain the on-site statutory registers, including the members' register; (2) update share/membership transfers in the court registry within 30 days of the underlying equity transaction; (3) if non-resident shareholders own a reportable foreign investment, submit the annual foreign-invested company business status report to KOTRA/MOTIE within 90 days after fiscal year-end; and (4) for AML/CFT purposes, conduct beneficial-owner due diligence and retain the records as required by the Financial Transaction Reports Act, reporting suspicious transactions to the Korean Financial Intelligence Unit (KoFIU). A dividend or distribution paid to a non-resident member is also subject to non-resident withholding tax and requires appropriate tax residency documentation.

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 24% top marginal rate; progressive schedule of 9% up to KRW 200 million, 19% between KRW 200 million and 20 billion, 21% between KRW 20 billion and 30 billion, 24% above KRW 30 billion
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: No statutory tax holiday for standard LLCs; available incentives include R&D expenditure tax credits up to 20% for eligible software/game-development SMEs and 10%-25% for large enterprises, plus foreign tax credit and tax deferral for certain digital content development expenditures; game publishing in-app purchase income is ordinary trading profit with no patent box regime

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Corporate Tax Base and Self-Assessment Return (Beobinse Gwaese Pyojun mit Seae Gyesanseo) filed through the National Tax Service HomeTax electronic filing portal
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Within 3 months after the end of the fiscal year (e.g., 31 March for a December 31 year-end corporation); an extension of up to 1 additional month may be requested through HomeTax for eligible foreign corporations

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Entity identification: legal name, business registration number, fiscal year, consolidated global income classification, residency status, and registered office address
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: For a Korean Yuhan Hoesa with non-resident shareholders, state foreign ownership percentage, attach foreign entity ownership schedules, and declare whether any foreign corporation has a Korean permanent establishment; in the year-end return, identify each non-resident shareholder for withholding certification purposes

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Gross revenue: all worldwide revenue from the MMORPG business, including in-app purchase proceeds, subscription fees, advertising, ancillary digital goods, and platform settlement amounts
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Include 100% of Apple App Store and Google Play end-user payments as gross revenue; deduct platform commissions as service charges only with valid invoices and platform payout statements; do not net platform fees against revenue unless arm's-length service agreements exist; reconcile foreign-currency settlement at the Korean Exchange Bank base rate

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Deductible expenses: game development costs, R&D wages, app store commissions, server hosting, marketing, royalty payments, intercompany fees, amortization of intellectual property, and general administrative expenses
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Royalty and service payments to non-residents must satisfy economic substance and transfer pricing arm's-length standards; add back expenses attributable to treaty-abused structures or undocumented foreign service invoices; if the foreign recipient was not subject to Korean withholding tax, enter gross-up adjustments and report the withholding liability in the supplementary withholding schedule

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Adjusted taxable income after add-backs and deductions: calculation of tax base from accounting profit after nondeductible expenses, tax-exempt items, prior-year deficit offset, and transfer pricing adjustments
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Disclose all transfer pricing adjustments made under the Adjustment of International Taxes Act, including CUP and TNMM recharacterization; apply upward adjustments to taxable income for intercompany royalty underpayments, excessive management fees, and artificial offshore payment constructs; for non-resident-controlled entities, document whether the Korean entity bears the core economic risk of the MMORPG platform

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Tax credits and final tax liability: foreign tax credit, R&D credits, employment credits, interim tax payments, gross income tax for certain branches, and withholdings previously paid on domestic income
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Claim foreign tax credit for foreign withholding or income tax paid abroad on revenue sourced through foreign subsidiaries only if the relevant foreign income is included in the Korean tax base; file Form 31 and supporting tax-paid certificates; any shortfall in additional corporate tax due after credits becomes the assessable liability subject to interest from the overdue date

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Non-resident tax declaration and withholding summary: dividends, interest, royalties, fees, and other outlet payments remitted to foreign shareholders or affiliates during the tax year
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Prepare a granular schedule showing each non-resident recipient, Tax Residency Certificate jurisdiction, beneficial owner status, country of residence, Korean withholding tax rate applied, DTA reduced rate claimed, application reference number, and proof of submission; if treaty relief was applied at source, attach the application under the Korea DTA; if relief was denied, report the withheld 22% amount and accrued penalties to avoid criminal exposure

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Sanctions for late filing, late payment, false declaration, and non-submission of supporting tax schedules
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Failure to file by statutory deadline: additional tax equal to 20% of unpaid tax (unfiled); negligent underreporting: 10% of the underreported amount; fraudulent underreporting or misreporting to gain treaty relief: 40% of underpaid tax; unpaid corporate tax interest accrues at 0.022% per day from the original due date; criminal tax evasion under the Punishment of Tax Evaders Act can result in imprisonment up to 10 years and fines up to 5 times the tax evaded

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late corporate tax filing imposes a 20% additional tax on the unfiled amount; negligent underreporting attracts a 10% surcharge; fraudulent underreporting (including false non-resident withholding declarations and treaty abuse) attracts a 40% surcharge; unpaid tax incurs 0.022% daily overdue interest; criminal evasion triggers imprisonment of up to 10 years and fines up to 5 times the tax evaded; failure to submit transfer pricing documentation separately attracts up to 30% adjustment penalties and evidentiary penalties under the Adjustment of International Taxes Act

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 22% default non-treaty withholding tax on outbound dividends (20% national corporate tax withholding plus 2% local income tax surtax); treaty relief may reduce this rate to 0%–15% depending on the relevant Double Taxation Agreement
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: To claim a reduced or zero DTA rate, the Korean withholding agent must obtain, before remittance, a Tax Residency Certificate (TRC) issued by the foreign tax authority, a completed Beneficial Ownership Declaration, and evidence that the non-resident shareholder/recipient has substantial activity rather than a shell conduit; the withholding agent must submit a withholding tax exemption or reduction application to the Korean National Tax Service (HomeTax) and receive approval before applying the treaty rate; if tax was withheld at the statutory 22% rate, the non-resident must file a domestic tax refund claim within the statutory period together with the TRC and BO declaration to obtain the treaty difference
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Statutory rates: 22% for both royalties (20% + 2% local surtax) and interest income of non-residents; under most Korean DTAs, royalties are commonly reduced to 10%–15% (rate may be 0% for some software/copyright royalties, but game-related digital royalties usually qualify as copyright royalties under the OECD Model), while interest is frequently reduced to 10%–15% with a possible 0% rate for specific state-owned lenders; procedural treaty relief remains mandatory for all outbound royalty and interest payments to non-residents

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: Mandatory Master File and Local File preparation and filing are required for cross-border related-party transactions when the aggregate annual value exceeds KRW 10 billion; below that threshold, contemporaneous TP documentation and set-the-price policies remain advisable as evidence under the Adjustment of International Taxes Act
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Korea does not apply a free-zone Economic Substance Regulations (ESR) regime, but the Korean tax authorities apply a rigorous economic-substance doctrine through judicial anti-abuse principles and the Adjustment of International Taxes Act: the Korean entity must demonstrate actual employees, servers, gameplay operations, contract enforcement capability, and decision-making in Korea as the Core Income-Generating Activities (CIGA) of the MMORPG platform; an offshore shell that bills all profits away from Korea without real activity will be disregarded, and profits will be reattributed to the Korean Yuhan Hoesa

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Directing Korean MMORPG in-app purchase receipts from Apple App Store and Google Play into an offshore nominee account, underreporting gross revenue, and failing to declare the global game publishing income in the Korean corporate income tax return
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Violation of the Punishment of Tax Evaders Act Article 3(1): imprisonment for up to 10 years or a fine up to 5 times the tax evaded; and an administrative 40% fraudulent underreporting surcharge under the Framework Act on National Taxes Article 47-3; the unpaid corporate tax and surcharge are immediately collectible by the National Tax Service
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Piercing the corporate veil: directors are jointly and severally liable to the Republic of Korea and the company under the Commercial Act Articles 389(3) and 399 for unpaid corporate tax and damages; the National Tax Service may seize personal bank accounts, real property, and personal passports, issue a travel ban (blacklisting) and denial of Korean tax clearance, and impose criminal imprisonment of the responsible director for up to 10 years

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Using a zero or low-tax jurisdiction holding company without employees, servers, or operational substance to invoice the Korean game IP royalties, receive dividends, and claim a fraudulent Double Taxation Agreement reduction on outbound dividends or royalties
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Denial of treaty benefits under the Adjustment of International Taxes Act Article 17(1) and recharacterization of the shell structure; the tax authority will reallocate income to the Korean entity and impose a 20% aggregate penalty on the adjusted transaction; unpaid withholding tax is reassessed at the statutory 22% plus daily overdue interest
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who approved or participated in the sham arrangement are personally liable for the unpaid non-resident withholding tax and penalties; the director may face a travel ban under the National Tax Collection Act, asset attachment, criminal liability for breach of trust under the Commercial Act Article 356, and imprisonment for up to 7 years if fraud against the company is established

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Transfer Pricing Documentation and False Intercompany Pricing
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Failing to prepare the mandatory Local File and Master File despite intercompany transactions exceeding KRW 10 billion, and setting artificial royalty, service, or interest rates for foreign affiliates without arm's-length benchmarking, thereby shifting profit offshore
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Under the Adjustment of International Taxes Act Article 13, the National Tax Service may adjust the intercompany price to an arm's-length value and impose an additional transfer pricing penalty of up to 30% of the adjusted income (10% if voluntarily corrected but late); failure to submit documentation separately attracts a penalty of 5% of the transaction value or KRW 100 million, whichever is greater
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Personal liability arises under the Commercial Act for directors who knowingly signed false tax returns and transfer pricing documentation; the National Tax Service can designate the director as a serious non-compliant taxpayer, impose a travel ban, order civil restitution for the additional tax and fines, and pursue criminal charges under the Punishment of Tax Evaders Act for willful falsification of documents, punishable by imprisonment up to 5 years and fines up to 10 times the false amount
